items.title: An immersion that is quasi-compact or has reduced source is an open immersion onto a scheme theoretically dense open of its scheme theoretic image
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for an immersion which is either quasi-compact or has reduced source, the induced morphism from the source to its scheme theoretic image is an open immersion identifying the source with a scheme theoretically dense open subscheme, and topologically dense as well (statement lines 1355-1363). The counted proof treats the two hypotheses separately: it factors the immersion into an open immersion followed by a closed immersion, uses minimality of the scheme theoretic image to place it inside the intermediate closed subscheme, and then either identifies the two closed subschemes by density together with reducedness and the criterion that a pointwise bijective closed immersion into a reduced scheme is an isomorphism, or quotes the two density assertions for the quasi-compact case (proof lines 1365-1387). It is H2: the case analysis is carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are the factorization and density statements of the same chapter.
